title: Choose the visual world
question: For a homelabber landing page, the roll assigned the Container Terminal direction. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Container Terminal
options.lineage: intermodal freight terminals & ISO container markings
options.thesis: Every workload is a sealed steel box on the yard; SwarmKit is the crane that places it.
options.viewport: A yard stack of corrugated containers under a gantry crane; each box carries a stencilled service ID and a lock state, the install command painted on the nearest door.
options.risk: Container wordplay reads on-the-nose unless the steel, stencils, and manifest are authored at full fidelity.

raised.raise: Monumental scale for the load-bearing figures: boot time and replica counts set as giant yard signage.
The crane arm and container locks draw on as you scroll, tracing the placement instead of fading in.
A calm single-column manifest inside the industrial frame, so dense copy reads like a bill of lading, not a poster.

options.label: Patch Panel & Link LEDs
options.lineage: homelab network racks, patch panels, and link LEDs
options.thesis: Each workload is a labelled port on the panel; isolation is a physical jack, not a shared kernel.
options.viewport: A 24-port panel fills the first viewport; ports light as services converge, the install command set in the legend strip.
options.risk: Familiar territory for infra pages — strong audience identification, real risk of blending in.

options.label: Seven-Segment Status Wall
options.lineage: seven-segment displays: clocks, price totems, scoreboards
options.thesis: Live counts in the display alphabet everyone reads — replicas, boot ms, health — with unlit cells drawn as deliberately as light.
options.viewport: A wall of seven-segment readouts: replica count, boot ms, nodes; each service a rigid mask of lit and unlit cells.
options.case: Fuses cleanly — counts map to segments and unlit cells carry state; loses narrowly on narrative.
options.risk: Reads retro-novelty if the mask is not strictly built.

options.label: Stencilled Label Grammar
options.thesis: Every zone named in literal straight quotes, hazard stripes under what matters, safety-orange tags for live state.
options.viewport: A labelled yard: each section plate reads its literal quoted name, one diagonal hazard stripe crossing the active row.
options.case: Fuses well — quoted literal labels make states self-explanatory; weaker on warmth.
options.risk: Novelty if the quote device is overused.

options.label: Tensegrity Force Column
options.thesis: Show the tension holding host and workloads apart: compression members are VMs, cords are the orchestration.
options.viewport: A force diagram in the first viewport; tracing a member follows its load to the counterforce, the host node pinned at the base.
options.case: Holds product clarity via engineering annotation; audience identification is thinner.
options.risk: Abstract — needs a literal reading to stay legible.

options.label: Command-Center Crisis Wall
options.thesis: A phosphor-orange control wall of counters and condition bars.
options.case: Loses on clarity and tone — a crisis wall implies alarms, and it is the category's own dark+neon default.

options.label: Hand-Drawn Zine Explainer
options.thesis: Explain the hard concept like a friend sketching it out.
options.case: Loses on audience identification — mascots and markers read beginner/consumer to infra operators.
options.kept: Draw-on reveal and the highlighter 'this line matters'.

options.label: Secession Ornament Page
options.thesis: An organic border grows inward, leaving a calm clearing for the text.
options.case: Loses on both axes — decorative ornament does not read as infrastructure.
options.kept: The calm single-column clearing inside the frame.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark hero with a terminal, a feature grid, and a comparison table, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
